object_description: long single-story school complex beneath a folding roof
design_condition: A long building is placed across the headland in the extension of the factory building, dividing the landscape into two areas while organizing gardens, courts, and sports space on either side.

positive.statement: The outdoor-space project integrates all required outdoor areas into a landscape-like design.
The intention to create a site-specific landscape developed from the stream-delta morphology is appreciated.
The tree population is carefully supplemented with new plantings that refer to the stream delta.
The two-level access opens repeatedly into spacious meeting areas in front of the school rooms.

negative.statement: The settlement produces a rather coincidental and structurally questionable division of the landscape.
The ramps are bottlenecks whose operational suitability is difficult to assess.
The architectural expression does not do justice to the sensitive setting and historic building structure.
The intended landscape theme is not successfully implemented beyond the level of the trees.
The oversized, surface-heavy square, promenade, and curved paths appear functional and lack spatial reference to the surrounding architecture.
The historic main building is not sufficiently integrated into the design of the square.
The length of the new house divides the landscape and prevents a flowing, coherent landscape.
There are doubts about the suitability of the concept from an operational perspective.
